findings.claim: Target UUIDs are serialized verbatim into fingerprints and route identities without canonical normalization, so alternate textual forms of the same UUID produce distinct locks and ledger identities for target-bound creation requests.

Changed intents add map entries without clearing the prior uncertain intent, and production mutation hooks do not invoke or expose cancel; returning to a previously abandoned payload therefore reuses its old key instead of establishing a new creation intent.

retainAfterFailure deletes the retained key for every ApiError, including the HTTP 409 produced while an identical command still holds the backend advisory lock; the next same-intent submission consequently uses a different idempotency identity while the original command may still complete.

Every HTTP error deletes the retained creation key. This includes the server idempotency_in_progress response while the original request may still complete; another submission then receives a new key and can execute as a separate creation.

Client intent identity trims and lowercases every string, while the server fingerprints the unnormalized decoded payload. Case or whitespace changes therefore reuse a key with a different server fingerprint, producing a conflict instead of a stable retry; subsequent key clearing permits a new creation identity.

Changing from unresolved intent A to intent B does not remove A's key from the map. Returning later to A reuses its stale key, so an earlier completed-but-unconfirmed creation can replay instead of executing the new intent.
The hook cancellation operation has no production call path: mutation hooks keep it local and expose only the React Query mutation result. Its sole invocation is in the hook unit test.

Commit tracking covers WriteHeader, Write, and ReadFrom, but Flush and Hijack delegate without marking the response committed. A panic after either capability causes recovery to attempt a 500 after commitment and records the wrong response status.

CanonicalTargetFingerprint serializes target strings unchanged; handlers also place raw path values into identity routes. The implementation therefore does not perform the target normalization asserted by its name, design, and specification.

The five idempotent creation handlers independently repeat key validation, transaction-service assertion, identity construction, authorization callback, command callback, response handling, and error translation. Identity and error handling already differ among copies.

Each RegisterRoutes models one executor as a variadic argument, silently selects only the first value, and switches creation routes to a different non-idempotent transaction path when omitted. The signature obscures a material transaction-boundary dependency.

Transactional creation paths duplicate authorization inside the command method and its separate AuthorizeTx method. The executor invokes two similarly named authorization boundaries in one transaction, while direct callers invoke only the command-side boundary.

PatchMember combines validation, transaction creation, lock ordering, requester authorization, owner-promotion policy, last-owner policy, removal, role update, and commit branches. Role normalization is repeated, making policy flow branch-dependent.

Hook and consumer names hide the lifecycle: retainAfterFailure performs no retention operation and instead deletes a key for ApiError; consumers call the object retry although it stores per-intent idempotency keys.

The test and completion evidence claim uncertain-failure retention, API-error clearing, and changed-intent reset, but the test never calls retainAfterFailure; its changed-intent assertion occurs only after explicit cancellation.
Operational and idempotency business rules are embedded as unrelated numeric literals for cleanup interval, batch size, retention, key limit, and created-only status.

Optional response-writer capabilities use unnamed bit values, a 16-way switch, and 15 near-duplicate wrappers, requiring capability meaning to be reconstructed across detector, switch, and declarations.

Delivery context is internally contradictory: design and exploration say exception approval is absent or pending and disagree on chained PRs, while tasks and apply-progress state that a size exception is approved.
Task 5.4 references Design section 18, but the design has no numbered section 18; task 5.1 also marks broader retry/reset evidence complete than the cited hook test exercises.
Fixture variables olderID and newerID cease to represent temporal order after timestamps are aligned; survivor assertions then depend on UUID ordering.
The hook returns cancel, but none of its production consumers call or expose it; only the hook test invokes it.
Two package-level blank-identifier declarations reference constructors already called earlier in the same file and have no remaining purpose.

Idempotency identities use raw target UUID path strings. Equivalent accepted UUID representations therefore acquire different locks and ledger identities, allowing the same canonical target and key to execute again instead of replaying.

Retry intent normalization lowercases every string while backend fingerprints preserve payload case. Case-only changes to case-sensitive group or workspace names reuse the previous key and can produce an idempotency conflict rather than represent a new intent.

Changing intent does not discard the prior intent retained key. Returning to an earlier payload in the same mounted mutation reuses its historical uncertain key instead of issuing the new key required for a new intent.

Flush and Hijack bypass statusWriter committed-state tracking. A panic after either operation is treated as uncommitted, causing an attempted JSON 500 and a recorded 500 after the response or connection was already committed.

No behavior test exercises creating a previously absent group grant and observing it after access-state refetch. Candidate tests only render a pre-existing grant or update and revoke one, leaving the stated creation contract unasserted.

Retry-key tests never exercise uncertain failure, ApiError clearing, or any production mutation request header. The changed mutation wiring externally visible retry contract is therefore not asserted.
